Read when merging completed slice findings. Write English `baseline/loss-analysis.md` or `iterations/iteration-N/loss-analysis.md`, bound to the evaluated AI/source. Review every newly played completed target loss; reuse only matching cached analysis.

Merge equivalent reasons globally. Include all groups affecting at least five distinct losses, ranked by count then severity; smaller groups enter neither final reasons nor replay jobs. Count a game once per reason, allowing overlaps. Preserve unclear losses and incomplete coverage. Judge visible information at the choice; identify supported mistakes without requiring proof an alternative wins before replay. Invent no attribution, gain estimates or confidence labels.

For every reason enumerate all affected games and primary critical decision IDs relative to the linked source evaluation. Link that evaluation once; qualify IDs if mixing evaluations. Replay points are required inputs, not a second loss ledger. Retain report and source records until all reasons are replay-processed and validation/reuse/resume needs end; apply the skill's Artifact lifecycle at closure.

Read before log review. `game.log` stores one game with actor A/B sections; `match.log` indexes four games and shared fixture/manifest metadata. Code reconstructs exact gameplay in memory; agents receive only target-loss projections.
- `o` and `a`: object and array containers, including empty ones.
- `s:"..."`: escaped string; JSON scalar escaping preserves tabs/newlines/quotes without making the record a JSON document.

Pre-side games mark sideboarding not applicable with empty exchanges. Game 3 records the transaction applied before play; game 4 marks that configuration carried forward. Exchanges list source/destination sections, card codes, quantities and reasons. Actors are stable identities, not starting seats. Each actor’s events contain only that actor’s legitimate observations; full game logs contain both perspectives for programmatic replay and must not be supplied directly to loss analysts.

`analysis-slices.ts` publishes `ASCENCIO_LOSS_LOG<TAB>2`: minimal identity, target sideboarding/initial state/events/result and end marker. Analysts receive only packet `jobs[].losses[].log` allowlists for completed target losses, never full two-actor logs or accepted winning gameplay.

5. Reuse only identity/hash-matching findings; verify IDs and exactly-once coverage. Wait for all slices, merge categories and compile the evaluation-bound [loss report](loss-analysis-template.md). Its global eligibility/ranking/replay-point contract governs; slice reports never independently trigger changes.

Write one row per target loss, fields separated by `|` with no pipes inside fields. Classifications: `avoidable`, `unavoidable`, `unclear`. An avoidable finding requires a decision ID present in that game's target record; use `-` when unavailable. The queue rejects wrong bindings, winning-game findings, duplicates, invented decisions and incomplete coverage. Human/agent findings and final reports remain Markdown. Regression diagnosis and isolated repair follow the skill’s Source selection and replay gate; observed associations are not causal proof.
